messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall @jamal for SEV2 — latency regression detected on /v1/generate (p50/p95 shifted). Auto-creation: incident 1893456789.
jamal: acked. I’m on it. Seeing sustained p50 ~120ms -> 220ms and p95 spiking from ~450ms -> ~1.4s across EU-West cluster since ~03:07 UTC. Some customer retries reported.
jamal: quick ask: anyone who touched node/kernel configs or infra since 02:30?
maria: I pushed a kernel livepatch to eu-west-canary at 02:58 (CVE backport). Not across full fleet yet. I’ll put the patch ops log here: https://internal.s3/redwood/ops/patches/1893456789.log
jamal: thanks. timeline looks like kernel change then latency shift ~9 mins later. Can we collect vmstat/perf on affected hosts?
maria: grabbing vmstat + /proc/vmstat from node eu-can-03. paste: 
```
03:12:05 vmstat -s
  1234567 K total memory
  987654 free memory
  765432 active
  543210 inactive
  1200 pages paged in
  580000 page reclaims
/proc/vmstat excerpt:
pgfault 184320
pgmajfault 312
pgfree 580000
```

maria: also saw kswapd CPU spikes in dmesg around 03:10.
kai: I pulled a few traces from trace-bucket (link: https://traces.internal/redwood/1893456789). Top-level spans show a repeated `io_wait` and `kv_cache_lookup` spans waiting on `page_fault` with heavy latency. Example trace span: `generate -> model.fetch -> kv_cache_lookup (wait_io: 800ms)`
kai: flamegraph snapshot (perf record -> perf script) indicates cycles in `kswapd` and `mm_fault_error` functions.
jamal: ok that's consistent with paging pressure hypothesis. Is this coming from THP/policy or kernel reclaim behavior introduced by the patch?
maria: the livepatch adjusted compaction heuristics for compaction_order. I have the commit id in the ops log.
sophia: adding metrics: host eu-can-03 minor_faults/min jumped from ~10/s to ~320/s at 03:07. major_faults also increased but lower absolute. context_switches up 3x.

sophia: vmstat (rolling 1m): r b  us sy id wa st  (r queue up)
03:05  1  0  65  10  20  5  0
03:09  12  4  70  12  10  6  0

jamal: mitigation options: 1) pin canary hosts to previous kernel; 2) disable THP on canary nodes (`echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled`); 3) increase node pool temporarily and route traffic away from hot hosts; 4) roll back livepatch. Which is fastest?
maria: fastest is routing traffic off eu-can-03 and pinning new canaries to prior kernel image. I can toggle THP too but unsure if it helps for our workload.
elaine: shifting traffic now: `/infra/route shift --from eu-can-03 --to eu-can-07,eu-can-09 --pct 100` -> command returned OK. Health checks: 10/10 passing on targets.

deploy-bot: kernel-pin action: image: redwood-kernel-5.15.84-prev applied to host group eu-canaries-pinned at 03:22 UTC (triggered by jamal).

jamal: after shift, p95 on /v1/generate dropped from ~1.4s -> ~480ms within 4 minutes (03:27). p50 back to ~180ms. Not fully resolved but better.
sophia: CPU on kswapd reduced, major faults trending down. pagefault rate halved.
kai: continued trace analysis: earlier traces show long tail in 'disk_read' inside page fault path; we may be hitting an edge-case where compaction increases latency for many small allocations and triggers synchronous disk reads.
maria: ops notes: livepatch changed compaction_order tunable from 2048->4096. rolling back that change on pinned hosts now.
jamal: hypotheses (in-thread):
- H1 (primary): livepatch changed compaction heuristics causing more aggressive background compaction -> increased page faults + kswapd contention -> elevated request latency (fits timeline).
- H2: THP/transparent hugepages interaction causing more major faults under our allocation pattern.
- H3: unrelated I/O regression coincidentally hitting same window (less likely given timing with patch).

jamal: experiments to validate: 1) Compare perf counters pre/post on pinned hosts (minor_faults, maj_faults, kswapd CPU). 2) Reproduce on staging by toggling compaction_order and running synthetic workload. 3) If reproduces, revert livepatch and coordinate a safe patch with the kernel team.

maria: I ran `perf stat -e minor-faults,major-faults,context-switches -a sleep 60` on eu-can-03 before rollback: 
```
 Performance counter stats for 'system-wide':
   192,345 minor-faults
     1,234 major-faults
   45,678 context-switches
```

maria: on pinned host after rollback: 
```
   12,876 minor-faults
     102 major-faults
   14,321 context-switches
```

jamal: that delta is large and supports H1. Good find.

elaine: handing off to night shift: I'll monitor traces and perf counters for next 12h. Summary for handoff -> continue collecting long-running perf + compare user-facing p95 per shard, keep routing policy in place if p95 stays >600ms on a host.

jamal: handoff checklist for elaine:
- links: ops log https://internal.s3/redwood/ops/patches/1893456789.log, traces https://traces.internal/redwood/1893456789, perf dumps https://internal.s3/redwood/perf/1893456789/
- current mitigations: pinned canaries to prev-kernel (group: eu-canaries-pinned), traffic shifted off eu-can-03.
- commands: `cat /proc/vmstat | egrep "pgfault|pgmajfault|pswpin|pswpout"`, `perf stat -e minor-faults,major-faults,context-switches -a sleep 60`, `bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:syscalls:sys_enter_open { @[comm] = count(); }' -p <pid>`
- desired next steps: run staging repro with toggled compaction_order and upload perf/trace as `perf_repro_{timestamp}.tgz` to perf bucket.

sophia: customer impact note: ~5% of active requests retried; a handful (3) enterprise customers reported visible slowness and one support ticket opened. No error rates increased.
jamal: tagging this incident SEV2-> investigating RCA. I'll open a postmortem doc and link when created. Assigning follow-up owners: kernel/release (maria), infra/runtime (jamal), traces (kai), customer comms (sophia).

elaine: acked, will pick up at 03:45 UTC. I'll post updates to this thread if I see re-emergence or if mitigations need escalation.

jamal: final for now — thanks all. leaving note: primary hypothesis H1 supported by perf stats and timeline. We'll run controlled staging test tomorrow to confirm and create patch w/ safer compaction defaults.

incident-bot: Incident 1893456789 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next: RCA doc required within 72h.
